## 3.1.1 Study MNTX 301 / MNTX 301EXT

The sponsor submitted two phase 3 studies to support the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous Methylnaltrexone (MNTX) sustained release (SR) in the treatment of opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced medical illness receiving palliative therapy.

design.text: Multi-center, single-dose, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study followed by a 28-day open-label period

citations.quote: Study 301 was a multi-center, single-dose, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study followed by a 28-day open-label period.

population.text: Patients with advanced medical illness (e.g. terminal illness such as incurable cancer or end-stage AIDS) and opioid-induced constipation, with a life expectancy of 1 to 6 months, who respond poorly to laxatives

citations.quote: This was a multi-center, single-dose, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group study in patients with opioid-induced constipation, and with an advanced medical illness (e.g. terminal illness such as incurable cancer or end-stage AIDS) and a life expectancy of 1 to 6 months.

endpoint.text: Proportion of patients with a rescue-free laxation response within 4 hours of the single double-blind treatment dose

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was a rescue-free laxation response within 4 hours of the single treatment dose (yes/no).

n.text: 154 patients treated in the double-blind period (47 RELISTOR 0.15 mg/kg, 55 RELISTOR 0.3 mg/kg, 52 placebo)

citations.quote: A total of 154 patients (47 RELISTOR 0.15 mg/kg, 55 RELISTOR 0.3 mg/kg, 52 placebo) were enrolled and treated in the double-blind period.

result.text: Laxation within 4 hours of the double-blind dose: 62% (0.15 mg/kg) and 58% (0.3 mg/kg) vs 14% placebo; p < 0.0001 for each dose versus placebo

citations.quote: RELISTOR-treated patients had a significantly higher rate of laxation within 4 hours of the double-blind dose (62% for 0.15 mg/kg and 58% for 0.3 mg/kg) than did placebo-treated patients (14%); p < 0.0001 for each dose versus placebo (Figure 1).
## 3.1.2 Study MNTX 302/ MNTX 302EXT
## 3.1.2 Study MNTX 302/ MNTX 302EXT

The sponsor submitted two phase 3 studies to support the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous Methylnaltrexone (MNTX) sustained release (SR) in the treatment of opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced medical illness receiving palliative therapy.

design.text: Two-week, multi-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group study of MNTX given every other day (QOD)

citations.quote: Study 302 was a two-week, multi-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled and parallel group study of MNTX 15 mg/kg.

- To determine the efficacy of MNTX at a dose of 0.15 mg/kg every other day (QOD) over a 1-week treatment period compared to placebo, in relieving opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced medical illness.

population.text: Patients from U.S. and Canadian sites aged 18 to 100 with advanced medical illness and opioid-induced constipation

citations.quote: The study included 174 subjects from U.S. and Canadian sites between the ages of 18 and 100 with advanced medical illness and opioid-induced constipation.

endpoint.text: Co-primary: proportion with rescue-free laxation within 4 hours after the first dose, and proportion with rescue-free laxation within 4 hours after at least two of the first four doses

citations.quote: The two co-primary efficacy endpoints of this study are: 1) the proportion of patients with a rescue-free laxation response within 4 hours after the first treatment dose (yes/no), and 2) the proportion of patients with a rescue-free laxation response within 4 hours after at least two of the first four treatment doses during the first week of double-blind treatment.
Data from 133 (62 RELISTOR, 71 placebo) patients were analyzed.

result.text: Laxation within 4 hours of the first dose: 48% RELISTOR vs 16% placebo (p < 0.0001); laxation within 4 hours after at least 2 of the first 4 doses: 52% vs 9% placebo (p < 0.0001)

citations.quote: RELISTOR-treated patients had a higher rate of laxation within 4 hours of the first dose (48%) than placebo-treated patients (16%); p < 0.0001 (Figure 1). RELISTOR-treated patients also had significantly higher rates of laxation within 4 hours after at least 2 of the first 4 doses (52%) than did placebo-treated patients (9%); p < 0.0001.

indication.text: RELISTOR is indicated for the treatment of opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced illness who are receiving palliative care, when response to laxative therapy has not been sufficient.

citations.quote: RELISTOR is indicated for the treatment of opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced illness who are receiving palliative care, when response to laxative therapy has not been sufficient. Use of RELISTOR beyond four months has not been studied.

target_moa.text: Methylnaltrexone bromide is a selective antagonist of opioid binding at the mu-opioid receptor; as a quaternary amine its ability to cross the blood-brain barrier is restricted, allowing it to function as a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist in tissues such as the gastrointestinal tract, decreasing the constipating effects of opioids without impacting central opioid-mediated analgesia.

citations.quote: Methylnaltrexone bromide is a selective antagonist of opioid binding at the mu-opioid receptor. As a quaternary amine, the ability of methylnaltrexone bromide to cross the blood-brain barrier is restricted. This allows methylnaltrexone bromide to function as a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist in tissues such as the gastrointestinal tract, thereby decreasing the constipating effects of opioids without impacting opioid-mediated analgesic effects on the central nervous system.

modality.text: Small molecule (quaternary amine derivative of naltrexone)

citations.quote: The chemical name for methylnaltrexone bromide is (R)-N-(cyclopropylmethyl) noroxymorphone methobromide. The molecular formula is C21H26NO4Br, and the molecular weight is 436.36.

key_safety.text: Most common (>5%) adverse reactions: abdominal pain 28.5% (vs 9.8% placebo), flatulence 13.3% (vs 5.7%), nausea 11.5% (vs 4.9%), dizziness 7.3% (vs 2.4%), and diarrhea 5.5% (vs 2.4%).

citations.quote: The most common (> 5%) adverse reactions reported with RELISTOR are abdominal pain, flatulence, nausea, dizziness and diarrhea. (6.1)

- **REMS/RiskMAPs:**
None were recommended.

vote.text: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred because the product is a member of the class of previously approved opioid receptor antagonists and did not pose unique concerns.

citations.quote: Your application for Relistor™ was not referred to an FDA advisory committee for the following reasons. Your product is a member of the class of previously approved opioid receptor antagonists marketed in the U.S., and the product did not pose unique concerns beyond those applicable to other opioid receptor antagonists.

detail.text: Approved effective on the date of the letter; the reviewers recommended approval with no prior Complete Response Letter stated.

requirement.text: Conduct a pharmacokinetics and safety study of Relistor in pediatric patients ages 5 to 17 years with opioid induced constipation and advanced illness receiving palliative care (required pediatric assessment under PREA; final report due December 31, 2010).

citations.quote: - Conduct a pharmacokinetics and safety study of Relistor™ in pediatric patients ages 5 to 17 years with opioid induced constipation and advanced illness receiving palliative care.

summary.text: Relistor was approved on a standard review cycle for opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced illness receiving palliative care; it was approved first cycle as recommended by the review team, without referral to an advisory committee, with one required pediatric postmarketing (PREA) study.
